name: BetaNYC/nyc-council-mcp
what_it_holds: MCP server for NYC Council legislative data pulled live via the Legistar API (bills, committee votes, hearing calendars). No stored dataset, but a working, current (updated July 2026) client scoped to exactly the council whose Local Law 18 (STR registration) most affects our NYC gap.
why_useful: Could pull the full NYC Council legislative history/amendments around Local Law 18 and any follow-on STR bills, useful context for interpreting the NYC Inside Airbnb dump gap (2023-06 to 2024-03) that gap #1 flags.

name: timmKal01/city-council-watch
what_it_holds: Apify actor (3 commits) that fetches newly filed ordinances/resolutions and upcoming council/committee agendas from any city's Legistar Web API given a city code as a parameter; no hardcoded city list or committed data, source/config/Dockerfile only.
why_useful: A generic, running scraper/method that could be filtered for STR-ordinance keywords across many US cities at once (LA, SF, Austin, Nashville, New Orleans, San Diego are all candidate Legistar cities in our Inside Airbnb panel), turning a one-off ordinance database into an always-on feed.
themes: STR regulation trackers and ordinance datasets: city STR law databases, Legistar/LegiScan clients, EU parliament open data, court records (CourtListener/RECAP) on Airbnb litigation
why_all: A generic, running scraper/method that could be filtered for STR-ordinance keywords across many US cities at once (LA, SF, Austin, Nashville, New Orleans, San Diego are all candidate Legistar cities in our Inside Airbnb panel), turning a one-off ordinance database into an always-on feed.

A generic, parameterizable way to monitor new STR-ordinance filings in near-real time across any Legistar city, which could catch new caps/bans as they are introduced ahead of the pitch deadline (gap #12); marginal given its small size and lack of committed data.

name: HowTheyVote/data
what_it_holds: Weekly-updated CSV.gz exports (votes.csv.gz, plus MEP and political-group tables) of every roll-call vote in the European Parliament, collected by howtheyvote.eu; downloadable via GitHub releases as a single export.zip, with pandas-ready examples in the README. 121 commits, actively maintained (weekly cadence).
why_useful: Machine-readable, point-in-time (weekly snapshot) EU Parliament vote history could locate/timestamp any EU-level short-term-rental or platform-economy (DAC7-adjacent) votes relevant to gap #12 (EU regulation trackers) and is a clean template for a point-in-time EU political-risk series (gap #4 vintage angle).

last_activity: actively maintained, weekly updates per README

name: opencivicdata/python-legistar-scraper
what_it_holds: A Python library (BSD-3, 52 stars, updated Aug 2026 — actively maintained) that scrapes any municipal Legistar site: agendas, bill/legislation text, votes, committee actions, meeting calendars. Legistar/Granicus is used by hundreds of US city councils.
why_useful: The core reusable client needed to pull city-council STR ordinance histories (hearing dates, vote counts, bill text links) for any of the ~40+ US cities that run Legistar (LA, SF, Boston, Chicago, Nashville, New Orleans, Austin, Denver, etc.) named in gap #12; complements the municipal registries we already hold with the legislative *process* record (when caps/bans were debated and passed).
time_coverage: as far back as each city's Legistar instance retains records (often 2000s-present)
themes: STR regulation trackers and ordinance datasets: city STR law databases, Legistar/LegiScan clients, EU parliament open data, court records (CourtListener/RECAP) on Airbnb litigation
wildcard: a regulator/compliance analyst tracking STR ordinances, regi
why_all: The core reusable client needed to pull city-council STR ordinance histories (hearing dates, vote counts, bill text links) for any of the ~40+ US cities that run Legistar (LA, SF, Boston, Chicago, Nashville, New Orleans, Austin, Denver, etc.) named in gap #12; complements the municipal registries we already hold with the legislative *process* record (when caps/bans were debated and passed).

A generic tool to build an STR-ordinance tracker across many US cities at once (introduction of registration caps, licence-fee hikes, short-term-rental bans/votes) — feeds CONTEXT.md gap #12 (STR ordinance trackers) and gap #17 (Socrata/CKAN-style open-data discovery is the analogue for civic legislative data). Method only, no data committed.
